prompts.text: What do you enjoy looking at first when you enter a local market?
Tell me about an unexpected conversation you had while shopping at a stall.
A market famous for fabric or one known for fresh produce?
Some stallholders remember regular customers by their usual order.
You're buying something at a market you've never visited. How do you decide which stall to try?
Which market smell tells you you're close before you see the stalls?
Market conversations sometimes teach more local slang than a language lesson.
Describe watching a vendor demonstrate something you didn't know how to use.
Your friend has ten minutes at your favourite market. What would you insist they see?
What do people in your area normally say when they leave a shop without buying anything?
What's an ordinary object at home whose story gets retold whenever somebody notices it?
Tell me about finding an old item and asking a relative why the family kept it.
A box of handwritten notes or a collection of old family photographs?
The objects people keep often reveal which memories they want close by.
You're choosing one small item to represent your family's everyday life today. What would you save?
Which piece of furniture has stayed in your family longer than anyone expected?
A well-used household item sometimes carries more history than an expensive souvenir.
Describe learning the story behind a gift somebody in your family has treasured for years.
An older relative offers to explain the history of one object in the house. Which would you point to?
What's something your family still uses in a way younger people find unusual?
